notes.summary: Time & Work questions are fastest with the LCM (total work) method. Pipes & cisterns use the same idea with emptying pipes as negative work. 1–2 questions per tier.

concepts.title: LCM method
concepts.body: Take total work = LCM of the days. Each person’s efficiency = total ÷ their days. Time together = total ÷ sum of efficiencies.

concepts.title: Man-days
concepts.body: Work = Men × Days × Hours. For the same work: M<sub>1</sub>D<sub>1</sub>H<sub>1</sub> = M<sub>2</sub>D<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub>.

concepts.title: Pipes & cisterns
concepts.body: Filling pipes do positive work; emptying pipes (leaks) do negative work. Net rate = sum of filling rates − sum of emptying rates.

example.q: A can do a job in 12 days and B in 24 days. Together?

varieties.name: Efficiency and man-days
varieties.how: Use M<sub>1</sub>D<sub>1</sub> = M<sub>2</sub>D<sub>2</sub>, or efficiency ratios.

example.q: 10 men finish a job in 6 days. How many days for 15 men?

varieties.name: Pipes and cisterns
varieties.how: Net rate = fill rates − empty rates; time = 1 / net rate.

example.q: Pipe A fills a tank in 4 h, pipe B empties it in 6 h. Both open?

tips: A is twice as efficient as B means A takes half the time.
Use the LCM of the days as total work to avoid fractions.
traps: If an emptying pipe is faster than the filling pipe, the tank never fills.
More men means fewer days: it is inverse proportion.

questions.q: A can complete a work in 10 days and B can complete it in 15 days. In how many days can they complete it together?
questions.solution:
Total work = LCM(10, 15) = 30 units.
A = 3 units/day, B = 2 units/day.
Together = 30/5 = 6 days.

questions.q: A pipe can fill a tank in 20 hours and another pipe can empty it in 30 hours. If both are opened together, in how many hours will the empty tank be filled?
12 men can complete a work in 18 days. In how many days can 8 men complete the same work?
A and B together can do a piece of work in 12 days. A alone can do it in 20 days. In how many days can B alone do it?
questions.solution:
B’s one-day work = 1/12 − 1/20 = (5 − 3)/60 = 1/30.
B alone takes 30 days.

questions.q: A is twice as efficient as B. Together they finish a work in 14 days. In how many days can A alone finish the work?
questions.solution:
Efficiency A : B = 2 : 1.
Total work = (2 + 1) × 14 = 42 units.
A alone = 42/2 = 21 days.

questions.q: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 hours and 15 hours respectively, while pipe C can empty it in 20 hours. If all three are opened together, in how many hours will the empty tank be full?
questions.solution:
Total = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units.
A = 5, B = 4, C = −3 units/hour → net 6 units/hour.
Time = 60/6 = 10 hours.
